A calendar failure rejects the mutation after persistence. All steps are verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

judged_text: The attendee DB write (lines 92-106) is followed by an unguarded 'await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees', so any calendar API failure rejects the mutation after the guests are already persisted. An expired calendar token turns the add into a 500 after partial persistence: attendees exist in the database but received no invite, and a retry with the same emails is rejected with BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', stranding the user in a state the UI cannot represent.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation persists new attendees first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., calendar credential/token failure), the TRPC mutation will reject after the DB write has already succeeded, leaving attendees persisted without the calendar update. On retry with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` filters out already-existing attendees and can become empty, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`), matching the described stranded state.
